title: Global State and Unsafe Traits
goal: Learn how mutable statics and unsafe traits require manual safety guarantees.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 4 Afternoon: Mutable Statics

sections.text: Global variables declared with `static mut` can be accessed by any thread at any time. Because Rust cannot prove at compile time that multi-threaded access is race-free, reading or writing a `static mut` requires an `unsafe` block.

sections.caption: Reading or writing a mutable static requires unsafe.

sections.text: In safe Rust, data races are prevented by ownership and borrowing rules. With `static mut`, you take full responsibility for thread synchronization.
Traits can also be marked `unsafe`. An `unsafe trait` declares that implementing it requires upholding invariants the compiler cannot verify. To implement such a trait, you must write `unsafe impl`.

sections.code:
unsafe trait ByteSerializable {}

unsafe impl ByteSerializable for Data {}
sections.caption: Implementing an unsafe trait requires the unsafe impl keyword.

sections.text: The built-in traits `Send` and `Sync` are unsafe traits. Marking a type `Send` promises that moving it across thread boundaries is safe, even if the compiler cannot verify it automatically.

explanation: Learn how mutable statics and unsafe traits require manual safety guarantees.
